source: Owner direct-chat clarification after inspecting ED-01 and discussing its surface and debris limitations
owner_message_original: Перебивание колонны насквозь и обрушение перекрытия это тут пока не нужно, эти колоны не будут рушаться, но я бы хотел, что бы достаточно хорошо осыпались и плитка и бетон. Как это впишется в наш текущий план?
owner_message_english_translation: Severing the column through and collapsing the ceiling are not needed here for now; these columns will not collapse, but I would like both tile and concrete to shed convincingly. How does this fit our current plan?
decision: Extend the planned first column specimen from removable cladding to locally breakable cladding and a bounded concrete surface volume over a permanent solid structural core. Columns and supported construction do not collapse.
planning_authority: Record this scope clarification in the existing MSQ-74 plan and prepared children. This conversation does not dispatch ED-02 or later implementation, approve candidate visuals, or extend the ED-01 review waiver.
planned_behavior: Actual localized repeated rifle hits can shed both cladding and exposed concrete, with material-specific fragments and persistent volumetric damage.
The concrete damage volume has a declared finite depth and leaves a permanent visible bullet-blocking core; no through-severing, column disappearance or ceiling collapse.
Retain the current selected column, original outer envelope and lab-only derivation boundary; do not expand into unselected walls, architecture or original/shared assets.

controller_plan_mapping.ED-02_MSQ-142: Layered local damage, concrete depth bounds, irregular fracture geometry and identifiable interior materials; basic large-fragment collision quality and explicit residual-core tests. Retain a separate selected thin witness specimen for through-shot evidence.
controller_plan_mapping.ED-03_MSQ-143: Stable cladding/concrete rubble, fragment interaction and sleep, bounded lifecycle, support and reset.
controller_plan_mapping.ED-04_MSQ-144: Reuse the layered authoring contract on a distinct selected specimen; two layers on one column do not alone satisfy the second-specimen requirement.
controller_plan_mapping.ED-05_MSQ-145: Increase density only after first-specimen fracture-surface and settling quality is demonstrated; measure both layers and accumulated rubble.
controller_plan_mapping.ED-06_MSQ-146: Material-specific dust, small chips and audio, plus presentation refinement and slowdown transitions; do not defer missing basic fracture surfaces or collision correctness to this stage.
controller_plan_mapping.ED-07_MSQ-147: Hand over the layered damage, exhausted-depth residual-core and settled-debris states with the existing technical and owner gates.

unresolved_tuning: Exact concrete damage depth, break thresholds, fragment distribution, impulses and active-body budgets require a measured candidate. The owner has not approved numeric values or physically exact ballistics.
preservation: Keep ED-01 Candidate01 and all historic approvals/evidence unchanged. Use task-owned lab derivatives and preserve original/shared assets and owner edits.
supersedes: For future planned work on the selected specimen, the requirement that all exposed concrete backing remain completely undamageable. Permanent structural continuity and shot blocking, no column collapse, no through-column witness test and all other laboratory boundaries remain in force.
